channel.title: Lynn Group Media - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Lynn Group Media (hoganstand.com)

item.title: Dublin and Galway to square off in Walsh Cup final
item.description: Dublin and Galway are set for a Walsh Cup final date next weekend after coming through their respective semi-finals in the Leinster pre-season competition this afternoon.

item.title: Monaghan to face Tyrone as McKenna Cup semi-finals set
item.description: Derry, Donegal, Monaghan and Tyroneare the last four teams standing the Dr McKenna Cup following this afternoon's results in the Ulster pre-season competition.

item.title: An Ghaeltacht see off Glenullin at Croker to secure All-Ireland club IFC crown
item.description: An Ghaeltacht (Kerry) are All-Ireland club intermediate football champions after a 0-12 to 0-6 win against Glenullin (Derry) at Croke Park this afternoon.

item.title: Sunday's club and inter-county results
item.description: Here are all of this afternoon's All-Ireland club final and pre-season inter-county results...

item.title: Clarke takes O'Mahonys reins
item.description: Former Louth sharpshooter Darren Clarke has been appointed manager of Meath football giants Navan O'Mahonys.

item.title: Pearses bolster management with Flynn appointment
item.description: Padraig Pearses would appear to be hellbent on knocking local rivals and All-Ireland club SFC finalists St Brigid's off their perch in Roscommon after adding Alan Flynn to their management team.

item.title: Glenullin boss laments below-par All-Ireland final display
item.description: A crestfallen Glenullin manager Michael O'Kane claims his team totally underperformed in their All-Ireland club IFC final defeat to An Ghealtacht.

item.title: Clogher rue missed chances and second half fadeout
item.description: Clogher manager Steven McKenna was left to rue missed first half goal chances and a disappointing second half display as his side came up short against Ballymacelligott in the All-Ireland club JFC final.

item.title: 'I'm sure dad would be very proud looking down'
item.description: Pádraig Ó Sé became the latest member of the famous Kerry football dynasty to win an All-Ireland medal at Croke Park yesterday.

item.title: 'Kerry are a good bit ahead of the chasing teams'
item.description: Brendan Devenney says Kerry are heading into the new season as favourites to retain their All-Ireland SFC crown.
